thesis: Collective action requires identifiable responsibilities and institutions without reducing everyone to identical guilt.

ideas.statement: Individual intervention probability differs from the probability that anyone helps; coordination can clarify diffuse duties.
A report needs a decision and verified outcome, with resources for its owner.
Present duties to repair common arrangements need not rest on inherited guilt.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Obedience can involve identification with a noble purpose, not merely blind compliance.
Neighborhood trust findings are observational, while solidarity can conceal abuse and cooperation requires material support.
Knowledge and influence constrain categorical public speech; institutions cannot presuppose ideal citizens.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Solidarity may protect abuse; collective efficacy evidence is observational.

audit.notes: All assigned units read. Claims remain bounded; hypothetical cases are not empirical evidence.
